findings.claim: SAFE-MAJ-001 and SAFE-MAJ-002 closures both add documentation-only enforcement whose trigger and content requirements can be circumvented by a malicious single-operator without independent review. The non-waivable 48h window in README.md fires only when §5 is non-empty; a malicious proposer can write 'None' in §5 (claiming no bypass surface) when there ARE implicit match-condition exclusions, and self-approve under quorum=1 without the window ever activating. The RULE-TEMPLATE §5 fourth prompt ('Implicit exclusion set') says 'Reviewers MUST verify the exemption set is intentional' — in single-operator mode the reviewer IS the author.
findings.evidence: README.md §Process step 2 lines 54–65: non-waivable trigger condition is 'any new .scp/rule-config.yaml key, any new scp_bypass: variant flag, any new per-finding waiver shape, OR any §5 implicit-exclusion set that wasn't named in a prior proposal'. If proposer writes 'None' in §5 (incorrect but undetectably wrong without independent review), the trigger evaluates false — standard 48h window applies and author can self-approve. RULE-TEMPLATE.md §5 lines 84–93: fourth prompt requests enumeration, default 'None' clause ('If the rule does NOT add a bypass surface, write None — uses existing scp_bypass three-gate + rule-config disable mechanisms') remains reachable for a proposer who defines §3.1 match conditions narrowly (affirmative-only firing) while answering §5 = 'None'. In single-operator mode (D-031: quorum=1, @jrnb2024 is the sole CODEOWNERS member), the quorum-1 approver IS the author — no second human evaluates whether §5 truthfully enumerates the implicit exclusion set. D-036 rationale inherits the D-031 posture without adding structural enforcement for the bypass-introducing-proposal path.
findings.impact: A malicious single-operator can draft a rule at threshold:warn whose §3.1 match condition fires only on an affirmative opt-in field (e.g., 'deny when services.yml key governance_enabled: true is present'), write §5='None', and self-approve within the standard 48h window. The rule ships to all adopters at threshold:warn; the opt-in-field absence is an unreviewed structural exclusion. When the rule is later promoted to threshold:deny (a separate MAJ proposal, also self-approvable in single-operator mode), the exclusion is established as shipped surface and changing it is breaking. This is NOT a new attack surface introduced by fix-round-1 — it is the acknowledged D-031 bus-factor-1 limitation. The closures are genuine improvements that close the gap for honest operators and create documented MUST obligations.
findings.mitigation: Structural fix requires multi-maintainer mode: when a second maintainer onboards at the 2026-07-21 quarterly review, flip require_review_from_non_author: true for bypass-introducing proposals per README.md's own forward-compat note. In the interim, a lightweight machine-readable signal could harden single-operator mode: add a YAML front-matter field to RULE-TEMPLATE (e.g., bypass_surface_non_empty: true|false) that a GitHub Action or PR-body bot can check — the 'None' claim would then be an explicit machine-readable assertion, making a false 'None' a flaggable discrepancy. This is forward-compat work (TF-020H1-005 scope or a new TF); no action required at v1.0.0 single-operator posture.

findings.claim: version-manifest.json at the repository root has no explicit CODEOWNERS rule. In single-operator mode (required_approving_review_count=0 per D-033) this is operationally inert. When a second maintainer onboards and review count flips to 1+, changes to version-manifest.json will not automatically request @jrnb2024 as a reviewer — a second maintainer could modify freshness_warning_threshold_minor without governance-owner review.
findings.evidence: CODEOWNERS file: rules enumerate policies/**, schemas/**, lib/**, .github/**, tests/**, renovate/**, docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/security/**, docs/adoption/**, docs/plans/**, docs/integrations/**, output/findings/**, output/control-tower/**, output/ci/**, scripts/**, vendor/**, /CODEOWNERS, docs/CODEOWNERS. No rule covers root-level files (no /* or /** wildcard). version-manifest.json sits at repo root. The file carries freshness_warning_threshold_minor, which post-SAFE-MIN-006 fix is the trust anchor for the freshness-warning threshold across all pinned wrappers. R1 cross_doc_consistency note already flagged: 'version-manifest.json at root has no explicit CODEOWNERS rule — any change to it routes through @jrnb2024 only because no other rule covers root-level files. In multi-maintainer mode this should be explicit.'
findings.impact: Low at v1.0.0 single-operator mode. In multi-maintainer mode: a second maintainer who gains write access could set freshness_warning_threshold_minor=0 (spurious SCP-FRESH-001 on every adopter PR run — warning fatigue; adopters may suppress the annotation, silencing legitimate future alerts) or threshold=9999 (silences warnings for all adopters, removing the signal that a security-relevant release is available). The PR + required-check pipeline still applies, so tampering requires a merged PR — not a silent push. CODEOWNERS ownership is the additional governance layer that would require @jrnb2024 specifically to review.
findings.mitigation: Add an explicit CODEOWNERS rule for version-manifest.json before the /CODEOWNERS self-protection line (per CODEOWNERS ordering invariant — specific rules must precede any future broad wildcard): `version-manifest.json @jrnb2024`. Alternatively, when a broad root-level wildcard is added for multi-maintainer coverage, ensure it precedes the specific governance lines per the ordering invariant. Track as forward-compat for second-maintainer onboarding event.

findings.claim: The preferred disclosure channel in SECURITY.md — GitHub Security Advisory at https://github.com/jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/security/advisories/new — cannot be verified as operational from read-only repository access. If the Private Vulnerability Reporting feature is not enabled on the repository, the URL returns a 404, and a reporter who cannot open the advisory may default to a public issue before trying the email fallback.
findings.evidence: SECURITY.md line 20: 'Open a private GitHub Security Advisory at https://github.com/jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/security/advisories/new. This is the preferred channel.' R2 instruction asks to verify via 'gh api repos/jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/security-advisories or check the repo Security tab' — read-only lens (Read/Grep/Glob only) cannot make API calls. GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting is a repository-level feature that must be explicitly enabled (available for public repos on personal accounts since 2022). The URL format is correct for GitHub's advisory endpoint with the repo's canonical trailing-dash name. Email fallback jimbrooke@me.com is always available and confirmed stable (memory user_james.md). ADOPT-001 §12.7.8 now references the same URL without 'when published' qualifier (correctly updated in fix-round-1). rule-regression.md comment block lines 33–34 also updated correctly.
findings.impact: Low. If the advisory URL is non-functional (feature not enabled), a reporter gets a GitHub 404 and may not immediately try the email path — creating a brief window before private disclosure is attempted. The practical blast radius is a single reporter's potential confusion, not a systemic bypass. The email fallback closes the gap.
findings.mitigation: One-time operator verification: run `gh api repos/jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/security-advisories` — a 200 response with [] or advisory list confirms the feature is enabled; a 404 or permission error means Private Vulnerability Reporting must be enabled via repo Settings → Security → Private vulnerability reporting → Enable. No code change needed. If confirmed enabled, this nit is resolved.

structured_review.summary: R2 SAFETY/BYPASS lens adversarial review on commit 3817384 (post fix-round-1). Scope: eight R1 findings, fix-round-1 closure genuineness, new attack surfaces from fix-round-1 edits, and missed attack classes. SAFE-MAJ-001 closure: the 'Bypass-introducing proposals — non-waivable 48h window' paragraph in README.md §Process step 2 adds a real procedural control. Adversarial test confirms the closure structurally relies on reviewer diligence to catch §5-vs-PR-description mismatch: a malicious proposer can write 'None' in §5 (hiding an implicit exclusion), write 'None' in the PR description, and self-approve — the non-waivable window never triggers because no §5 non-empty flag is set. This is the acknowledged D-031 bus-factor-1 ceiling in single-operator mode (MIN residual, not a new MAJ). SAFE-MAJ-002 closure: the §5 fourth prompt ('Implicit exclusion set') forces enumeration by guidance + MUST-level requirement, not by structure — the default 'None' answer remains available and a proposer who answers it when there ARE match-condition exclusions violates the template but in single-operator mode no independent reviewer catches the omission. Same D-031 residual (folded into R2-SAFE-MIN-001). SAFE-MAJ-003 closure: SECURITY.md present at repo root (66 lines), both channels documented, cross-references updated in rule-regression template and ADOPT-001 §12.7.8 (both drop 'when published'). Fix-round-1 new surfaces: Python str.replace() is non-evaluating (sound); :- operator on SCP_REGRESSION_ASSIGNEES handles empty string (sound); concurrency cancel-in-progress:false queue exhaustion bounded by write-permission requirement (sound); release trigger weaponisation bounded by write-permission requirement (sound); D-036 formalises existing D-031 posture without adding bypass surface (sound). Two new minor/nit findings: CODEOWNERS missing explicit rule for version-manifest.json at repo root (forward-compat nit); GitHub Security Advisory URL operability unverifiable from read-only access (nit; email fallback confirmed).
structured_review.verdict_rationale: Zero new CRIT or MAJ findings — fixpoint criterion met. All three R1 MAJ closures verified as genuine: SAFE-MAJ-001 adds a real procedural control (non-waivable 48h window + mandatory PR-description bypass enumeration); SAFE-MAJ-002 adds a real structural prompt with a MUST-level requirement; SAFE-MAJ-003 ships a complete SECURITY.md stub with both preferred and fallback channels, SLA, and coordinated-disclosure window. All five R1 MIN/nit closures verified sound: Python heredoc (SAFE-MIN-004) is injection-safe; threshold read from pinned manifest (SAFE-MIN-006); assignee env-default handles empty-string correctly (nit-007); §10 BLOCKING-vs-deferrable markers added (nit-008); rule-config canary gap tracked as TF-020H1-004 (SAFE-MIN-005). No new attack surfaces introduced by fix-round-1 edits. Two residual findings (1 MIN, 2 nit): documentation-only enforcement in single-operator mode is the acknowledged D-031 bus-factor-1 ceiling, not a new surface; version-manifest.json CODEOWNERS gap is a forward-compat nit; GitHub Security Advisory URL operability is unverifiable from read-only access.
